name: Chronotek Signal-Blocking Watch Case
description:
A wrist-worn case that holds a standard smartwatch or comm device inside a Faraday-shielded enclosure. When closed, the device inside is completely invisible to all wireless scanning. When opened, the device functions normally. The case adds about 8mm of bulk to the wrist profile.

Carried by individuals who want their connected devices accessible but not broadcasting their location at all times. Closing the case is a conscious act of disappearing from the network — opening it is a conscious act of returning. The ritual of choosing when to be visible gives the wearer a sense of control in a city where surveillance is ambient.
functionality: Selective device signal blocking, Faraday enclosure, manual visibility toggle
what_it_says: You decide when the network knows where you are, and you carry that decision on your wrist.
story_hooks: A Signal-Blocking Watch Case is found open on a desk — the device inside was broadcasting location data for exactly seven minutes before the case was closed again, a window that matches the duration of an encrypted data transfer from the same building.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, angular wrist cuff with a hinged clamshell design that wraps around the wrist. When closed, it presents as a sleek, minimalist bracelet with no visible seams or openings. When open, it reveals a recessed pocket holding a smartwatch or comm device. The overall silhouette suggests purposeful restraint—less jewelry, more instrument.
physical_description.fit: Snug against the wrist with adjustable friction-fit bands; adds approximately 8mm of bulk to the wrist profile without feeling heavy or obstructive. Sits between fitted watch and rigid cuff.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte-finished ballistic composite with internal copper-mesh Faraday shielding; exterior shell is treated graphene-reinforced polymer.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost matte on the exterior with subtle micro-etching; internal pocket surfaces show fine mesh pattern from shielding layer. Hinges are precision-machined and feel deliberate when operated.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray or charcoal black as standard; accent details in dull copper or bronze where Faraday mesh is visible through thin gaps. Some units feature burnt orange accent lines along hinge seams.
physical_description.closures: Precision magnetic snap closure with tactile detent feedback; opens with deliberate pressure, closes with a distinct 'lock' sensation. Dual-stage magnets prevent accidental opening.
distinctive_features: Visible hinge mechanism with precision-machined aesthetic
Minimal branding—small Chronotek logomark on clasp
Interior pocket sized for standard 44mm smartwatch faces
Micro-ventilation holes to prevent condensation buildup
Custom etching options for owner identification or deadpan slogans ('OFF THE GRID,' 'GHOSTING,' 'SIGNAL DENIED')
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2–3 boundary. Expensive enough to signal deliberate privacy consciousness; practical enough for working-class street operators. Not luxury, not budget—specialized tool.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by corporate security specialists who need selective connectivity, street informants avoiding corpo tracking, medical workers managing data sensitivity, and privacy advocates making a statement. Signals distrust of ambient surveillance and preference for controlled visibility. Also popular among underground network operators and black-market couriers.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new; develops subtle micro-scratches on the exterior with age. Internal mesh occasionally shows fine dust accumulation visible through seams (cosmetic only). Magnetic snaps may show faint wear marks from repeated opening. Well-maintained units look intentional and deliberate; neglected ones look paranoid.
